keyVerseText: Behold, therefore I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and will deliver thee for a spoil to the heathen; and I will cut thee off from the people, and I will cause thee to perish out of the countries: I will destroy thee; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD. a spoil: or, meat
rootMeaning: The word בַּג (bag) is a masculine Hebrew noun of Persian origin, indicating a loanword that entered the Hebrew lexicon. Its core meaning revolves around 'spoil' or 'booty,' specifically referring to food or goods taken as plunder. The etymology as a Persian term suggests a cultural borrowing that emphasizes the tangible, material aspect of spoilage or captured goods, enriching the Hebrew concept beyond a generic term for spoil to include the idea of sustenance or meat.
usageInScripture: This word appears only once in the Hebrew Bible, specifically in Ezekiel 25:7, where it is used in the context of spoil or booty taken by heathen nations. The lexicon note indicates that the Masoretic text reads בַּז (baz), linking it to a root meaning related to plundering or spoiling. The consistent translation as spoil or meat in this verse highlights its use as tangible goods taken in conquest or judgment, emphasizing the physical consequences of divine punishment.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding בַּג as spoil or booty deepens our grasp of divine judgment language in Scripture, where God's hand is portrayed as delivering nations into the hands of others for destruction and plunder. This word vividly illustrates the reality of God's justice—where sin leads to ruin and loss, not merely abstract punishment but tangible consequences. For the Christian faith, it underscores the seriousness of rebellion against God and the certainty of His sovereign judgment, while also pointing to the hope of restoration when God’s purposes prevail. The material nature of spoil also reminds believers of the transient nature of worldly gains compared to eternal spiritual riches.
keyVerseReflection: Ezekiel 25:7 declares, 'Behold, therefore I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and will deliver thee for a spoil to the heathen...,' using בַּג to signify the tangible consequences of God's judgment. The word 'spoil' here conveys the complete defeat and despoiling of the judged nation, emphasizing the severity of God's wrath. This term enriches the verse by highlighting not only destruction but the handing over to others for plunder, illustrating the totality of divine retribution and the loss that follows rebellion against the LORD.
